speaker_role: essay coach / founder of College Essay Guy; says he has read thousands of essays
commercial_incentive: Runs a company with paid resources and coaching; points viewers to his website.
key_insights: Ignore the Common App prompts at the start; brainstorm inward on what you can offer rather than what readers want.
For montage essays, favor topics that are elastic (can show many sides of you) and somewhat uncommon.
For narrative essays, judge whether the challenge is compelling and whether the insight is fresh; strong craft or improved insight can rescue a modest challenge.
Common topics like sports, clubs and service are harder to stand out with; save activities for activity-focused supplements.
Five things exercise: list five linked objects or places, each revealing a different facet, and state the frame early.
21 details exercise: write many random facts; odd ones later in the list often become topics, including for supplements.
'I love' exercise: list loves and knowledge areas, which often yield elastic topics such as pranks.
Do not overthink; outline or draft for about 20 minutes to test a topic.
specific_numbers_or_facts: Suggests 5 to 10 minutes per brainstorming exercise and aiming for 21 details.
Speaker explicitly says the topic-quality grid reflects his own biases, not all readers.
notable_or_distinctive: Offers a two-axis (elasticity vs. commonness) test for topics and concrete exercises with example essay openings.
reliability_notes: Presented as personal opinion based on coaching experience, not admissions-office data; auto-captions mostly clean.
